news.summary: SpaceX announced plans for two AI supercomputing campuses worth more than $74 billion: up to $24 billion at its Starbase site in Texas and roughly $50 billion in Cochise County, Arizona, where the campus could eventually draw up to 6 gigawatts. The Texas facility would generate its own electricity, while the Arizona campus would work with local electric cooperatives.
news.title: SpaceX plans more than $74 billion of AI supercomputing campuses in Texas and Arizona
news.why: A rocket company now plans to spend more on AI computing than most countries, and its AI segment already brings in over half of SpaceX's revenue — but both campuses still need local approvals, with hearings and votes scheduled for December 9, so the $74 billion is an announced plan, not a construction site.

news.summary: British AI chip startup Fractile raised more than £500 million in a Series C round valuing the company at over £5 billion, with the UK government's Sovereign AI Venture Fund and the British Business Bank joining investors including CapitalG, Lightspeed and Redpoint. Fractile designs chips meant to run AI models faster, cheaper and more energy-efficiently, and its first chip has not shipped yet.
news.title: British AI chip startup Fractile raises over £500 million at a valuation above £5 billion
news.why: The round makes Fractile one of Britain's most valuable AI hardware bets, but the government's own notes say its typical cheques run £1–10 million — a small slice of a £500 million round — so the state's role is an endorsement, not the financing, and a valuation is not revenue.

news.summary: OpenAI launched ChatGPT Wallet, which lets AI agents shop and check out on a user's behalf, starting with a limited rollout to U.S. Pro subscribers.
news.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Wallet, letting AI agents shop and check out for you
news.why: It moves agents from answering questions to spending money, raising the stakes on mistakes and fraud — and a limited rollout is not proof most users will hand their card to an agent.

news.summary: LangChain raised $300 million in a Series C round led by existing investor CapitalG, at a $3 billion valuation. The money backs LangSmith, its platform for operating, improving and governing AI agents.
news.title: LangChain raises $300M Series C at $3B valuation for agent governance
news.why: A $3 billion valuation signals investors believe agent tooling is a real business — not that LangChain is profitable, or that agents are reliable enough to govern yet.

news.summary: Anthropic released Claude for Manufacturing, a plugin that connects Claude to factory software such as Autodesk Fusion, Oracle NetSuite and Infor. Its 17 skills can draft quotes, compare suppliers and place backup orders when deliveries slip, after human approval.
news.title: Anthropic's Claude for Manufacturing plugs AI into factory software
news.why: It shows frontier models moving into industrial workflows — but the plugin does not control physical machinery, and factory adoption is still unproven.

news.summary: Google is rolling out a Google Wallet connection for all Gemini app users in the United States, letting them ask personal-finance questions informed by their spending and, optionally, data from linked bank and credit-card accounts.
news.title: Google adds Google Wallet spending insights to the Gemini app
news.why: It makes Gemini more personally useful — but it also means more financial data flowing into Google's AI, and opt-in convenience is not the same as a privacy guarantee.

news.summary: DeepSeek opened the capabilities behind its consumer app — web search, file reading, voice and safety checks — through its API, so developers can build a chatbot that behaves like the DeepSeek app. It also published an open-source chat demo that can import conversation history from the app.
news.title: DeepSeek turns its whole app into an API, with search, file reading and voice built in
news.why: It lowers the work needed to clone a full-featured chatbot — but the documentation states no prices or rate limits, and public-facing services must handle their own compliance.

news.summary: Nearly 70 percent of US government agencies use generative AI, and public-sector unions are increasingly pushing through protections against AI surveillance and automated firings. In Oakland, a strike vote forced retraining instead of layoffs, and California banned so-called bossware.
news.title: Nearly 70 percent of US agencies use generative AI, and unions are catching up with guardrails
news.why: Adoption in government is already widespread — but usage is not the same as governed, reliable deployment, and the guardrails are still being negotiated.

news.summary: Google released Gemini 4 Hydrogen on November 12, a faster, cheaper member of the Gemini 4 family built for coding and multi-step agent work. It is rolling out across the Gemini API, AI Studio, the Gemini app and Search, priced at $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens.
news.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a faster model for coding and agents
news.why: It puts a near-frontier model in front of everyday users and developers at a low price, but Google's speed and benchmark claims are its own and have not yet been independently reproduced.

news.summary: Anthropic opened a private beta of self-hosted Claude Managed Agents, letting companies run the whole agent service — harness, sandboxes, credentials and session history — inside their own cloud or data centre. Model calls still go to a provider the customer picks, Anthropic by default.
news.title: Anthropic lets companies run Claude Managed Agents on their own servers
news.why: It removes a big reason regulated companies kept agents out of their systems, but it is a private beta with no public price or general-availability date, and it moves the control plane home, not the model itself.

news.summary: Four nonprofit groups sued OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta and SpaceX's AI division in a California court on November 12, asking a judge to bar the labs from building or deploying AI systems more capable than their current ones. The suit cites the companies' own warnings about extreme AI risks.
news.title: Nonprofits sue five AI labs seeking a halt to frontier model development
news.why: A court-ordered freeze would be a first for the industry, but this is a filing, not a ruling — no freeze has been ordered, no hearing date set, and none of the companies has responded.

news.summary: OpenAI introduced two Daybreak security products at its Cyber at the Frontier event: Red Team, which sends agents to probe web apps for vulnerabilities, and Defense Factory, which traces flaws through code and drafts patches for engineers to review. Red Team is in early access.
news.title: OpenAI launches Daybreak Red Team and Defense Factory security tools
news.why: It turns AI security testing from a one-off exercise into a continuous service, but OpenAI has published no pricing or independent results, and every patch still needs a human engineer to approve it.
